To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic control of a quantitative delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to mycobacteria is localized in 2 regions of the human genome that have been previously linked with mycobacterial infection.

genomewide linkage analysis in families of Vietnamese patients with leprosy identified 2 chromosomal regions (2q35 and17q21) that were linked to the Mitsuda reaction, which is a granulomatous reaction induced by mycobacterial infections.

genomewide linkage analyses of the granuloma-forming capacity in leprosy families identified 2 chromosomal loci (on 2q35 [P = 9.3 x 10(-3) at SLC11A] and 17q [P = 8.3 x 1 0(-3)]) that are likely to be involved in the development of granulomas.
